cards.text: This is a letter from Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James. He writes to those who are called, loved by God the Father, and kept in Jesus Christ. Friend, if my mail ever came addressed like that, I'd frame the envelope and hang it over the oven.
Then he writes, "Mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you." That's the difference between one cookie and a full tray, friend.
Jude says he'd made every effort to write to them about the salvation they share. But now he feels it's NECESSARY to write something else.

cards.question: Jude says he felt it necessary to urge them to ___ earnestly for the faith.
Jude says this faith was entrusted to the saints once for all. What does that tell you about it?

answers.text: It changes with every new leader

cards.text: Here's why: certain men have crept in among them unnoticed. Like ants in the cookie box, nobody EVER sees the first one walk in.

cards.question: Jude says these ungodly men were designated long ago for condemnation. What do they turn the grace of our God into?
Jude says the men who crept in deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Jude says they're fully aware of all this, but he's going to remind them anyway, starting with the people Jesus delivered out of the land of Egypt. That's me and my oven timer, friend: I KNOW, and I still need the beep.

cards.question: Jude says that after Jesus delivered His people out of Egypt, He let those who did not believe go unpunished.

cards.text: Next reminder: the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling.

cards.question: Those angels are bound for judgment on that great day. Where are they being kept until then?

answers.text: In a pit out in the wilderness
In the lions' den in Babylon

cards.text: Then Jude points to Sodom and Gomorrah, cities the LORD rained fire on (Genesis 19:24), and the cities around them. They indulged in sexual immorality and pursued strange flesh.

cards.question: Jude says Sodom and Gomorrah are on display as an ___ of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.

cards.text: Now Jude swings back to the men who crept in and calls them dreamers. In the same way, they defile their bodies, reject authority, and slander glorious beings.
But compare that to Michael, the archangel, who once got into a dispute with the devil himself. The DEVIL, friend, the one guy who's got every hard word in the world coming to him.

cards.question: What were Michael the archangel and the devil disputing over?
Even with the devil, Michael did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him. So what does Michael say?
Michael would not bring a slanderous charge, even against the devil. Jude says the men who crept in understand the things they slander.

cards.text: They slander what they do not understand. And like irrational animals, they will be destroyed by the things they do instinctively.
"Woe to them!" Jude says. First, these men have traveled the path of Cain, Adam's son who killed his brother Abel (Gen 4:1, 8).
Next comes Balaam, a man hired to curse Israel (Deut 23:4).

cards.question: Jude says these men have rushed into the error of Balaam. What did they rush for?

cards.text: And last comes Korah, who rose up against Moses (Num 16:1-3).

cards.question: Jude says these men have perished in Korah's rebellion.

cards.text: Then Jude paints these men in pictures. They're hidden reefs in their love feasts, shamelessly feasting with them.

cards.question: These men feast shamelessly at the love feasts. But who does Jude say they are shepherding?

cards.text: Next picture: they're clouds without water, carried along by the wind. Wherever the wind goes, they go, like the parchment paper every time somebody swings the bakery door OPEN.

cards.question: Jude also pictures these men as trees in autumn. What does he say about those trees?

cards.text: In fact, Jude says those trees are twice dead after being uprooted. And these men are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame.

cards.question: Jude calls these men wandering stars. What has been reserved for them forever?

cards.text: Then Jude brings in Enoch, the seventh from Adam, a man who walked with God (Gen 5:24). Jude says Enoch prophesied about these men, so they were getting talked about way, WAY back.

cards.question: In Enoch's prophecy, who is coming with myriads of holy ones?
Enoch says the Lord will convict the ungodly of their wicked acts, but not of the harsh words they spoke against Him.

cards.text: Jude piles it on: these men are discontented grumblers, and their mouths spew arrogance. Friend, grumbling AND bragging at the same time takes STAMINA.

cards.question: These grumblers follow after their own lusts, and they ___ others for their own advantage.

cards.text: Then Jude turns back to his readers, the beloved, and tells them to remember what the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ foretold. Basically, friend: you were WARNED about these guys.

cards.question: What did the apostles say there would be in the last times?

answers.text: Scoffers following their own ungodly desires
A great famine across the land

cards.question: Jude says these scoffers are the ones who bring believers together.

cards.text: These scoffers are worldly and devoid of the Spirit. But Jude hands the beloved a recipe: build yourselves up in your most holy faith, and pray in the Holy Spirit.

cards.question: As they build themselves up and pray, Jude tells them to keep themselves in the ___ of God.
While they keep themselves in God's love, what does Jude say they are waiting for?

answers.text: The mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ
A new letter from the apostles
The temple to be built again

cards.text: And that mercy will bring them eternal life. Then Jude points them outward, toward other people, and not everybody gets the same thing from them.

cards.question: How does Jude tell them to respond to those who doubt?
Others, Jude says, they should save by snatching them from the ___.

cards.text: And to still others, they show mercy tempered with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
Jude doesn't end on a warning but on praise to the One who is able to keep them from stumbling. Friend, I hop around this bakery on a gold base all day, so believe me, I APPRECIATE that.

cards.question: Jude says God is able to present them in His glorious presence. How?
Jude's closing says to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority for all eternity.

cards.text: And all of it comes through Jesus Christ our Lord. Jude closes his letter with one word: Amen.
